key_highlights: ASX treads water amid persistent interest-rate fears; RBA Governor Bullock's hawkish stance reinforces 'higher for longer' narrative
Iron ore downside risk persists, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX valuations
Sydney housing market under severe stress; auction market facing reality check
Active WA/SA/NSW gold exploration (Platina, Broken Hill, Larvotto, Great Southern, Forrestania) signals sector resilience
Chevron and ExxonMobil double down on LNG, supporting energy sector capex cycle
Super contributions surge >33% post-budget tax changes; government-backed digital pension scheme proposed
Consumer weakness flagged: Dollar General CEO red flag, Christmas retailer Chapter 11, discount fashion chain closing 120 stores
Trump-Xi summit anticipation lifts global equities; China economic cracks add geopolitical risk
Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire chairman at 96, marking generational shift in global investing

sectors.trend: Iron ore weakness persists; gold exploration active across WA, SA, NSW; rare earths (Dalaroo) and antimony (Larvotto) gaining traction
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from iron ore downside; gold juniors (Platina, Broken Hill, Great Southern, Forrestania) offer speculative upside; Dalaroo rare earths play benefits from China supply-chain decoupling

sectors.trend: Higher-for-longer rates support NIM but housing stress (Sydney bloodbath, auction reality check) threatens credit quality; super contributions surge boosts fund flows
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from rate environment but face rising NPL risk in residential mortgages; super fund managers see inflow tailwind

sectors.trend: Chevron/ExxonMobil LNG capex doubling; diesel/petrol price shock rising; EV adoption accelerating in Australia
sectors.implications: Woodside.AX, Santos.AX, Chevron.AX benefit from LNG investment cycle; fuel-cost inflation pressures consumer sector; EV transition long-term structural shift

sectors.trend: Consumer confidence deteriorating: Dollar General CEO warning, Christmas retailer bankruptcy, discount fashion chain closing 120 stores
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX, IAG.AX face margin pressure; defensive consumer staples (WOW.AX, AGL.AX) preferred; retail sector under structural stress

sectors.trend: Novo Nordisk pipeline concerns weigh on global pharma; NDIS funding failures highlight domestic healthcare gaps
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, COH.AX relatively insulated but global biotech sentiment negative; NDIS policy risk for aged-care providers

sectors.trend: Contributions surge >33% post-budget; government-backed digital pension scheme proposed; system fitness questioned
sectors.implications: Super fund managers (HUB.L, PPU.AX, QAN.AX) see AUM growth; potential regulatory disruption from parallel pension scheme

key_themes: RBA hawkish bias (Bullock) and 'higher rates as new normal' dominate rate-sensitive sectors
Iron ore structural downside vs. gold/rare earths exploration boom
Housing market correction in Sydney and nationally
Consumer spending weakness across retail and discretionary
LNG capex super-cycle supports energy majors
Superannuation reform and digital pension innovation
Trump-Xi summit and China economic fragility as global risk
Generational leadership shift (Buffett exit) in global markets

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds; favour banks with strong NIM; underweight rate-sensitive REITs and growth equities
Reduce exposure to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; rotate into gold and rare earths names
Monitor bank NPL trends; underweight residential REITs; favour commercial/industrial REITs
Shift to defensive staples (WOW.AX, AGL.AX); avoid discretionary retail exposure
Hedge commodity exposure; monitor AUD/USD; diversify away from China-dependent exporters
Favour EV-transition beneficiaries; monitor transport and logistics cost pressures

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold exploration and production names
opportunities.rationale: Active drilling results (10.72g/t Great Southern, Broken Hill uplift, Larvotto first concentrate) signal sector momentum; gold hedges rate uncertainty

opportunities.recommendation: Add LNG-exposed energy majors on capex cycle
opportunities.rationale: Chevron/ExxonMobil doubling LNG investment supports Woodside and Santos through 2028+; Brookfield $5B transition fund adds infrastructure demand

opportunities.recommendation: Position in rare earths / critical minerals
opportunities.rationale: Dalaroo Greenland rare earths breakthrough plus China supply-chain decoupling theme supports structural demand

opportunities.recommendation: Favour banks with strong NIM and diversified lending
opportunities.rationale: Higher rates support earnings; super contribution surge boosts fund flows; CBA best positioned for credit resilience

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore / thermal coal exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Persistent iron ore downside and China demand weakness cap upside for BHP, RIO, FMG

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight residential REITs and rate-sensitive growth
defensive_moves.rationale: Sydney housing bloodbath and higher-for-longer rates pressure valuations and occupancy

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim discretionary consumer and retail exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Consumer red flags (Dollar General, Christmas retailer bankruptcy, fashion closures) signal demand erosion

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain AUD/USD hedge on commodity export exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: China weakness and Trump trade policy create AUD downside risk

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound ('treading water') as rate fears and iron ore weakness offset gold/energy strength. Trump-Xi summit outcome is key swing factor. Housing data and RBA commentary will dominate. Expect volatility around 8,200–8,600 ^AORD.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural shift toward critical minerals, LNG, and energy transition supports selective outperformance. Housing correction and consumer softness cap broad-market upside. Superannuation reform and digital pension scheme could reshape financial sector flows over 12 months. Buffett's exit signals a new era of passive/index investing dominance.
